v2.2.0 (New version)
Smart cubes
  • Cubench now connects to GAN, MoYu and QiYi Bluetooth smart cubes
  • The timer starts on your first turn and stops when the cube is solved
  • The scramble follows your turns, and a wrong move is caught and corrected
  • Every solve is split into its steps (cross, F2L pairs, OLL, PLL), with thinking and turning times and the full reconstruction
  • Any solve can be replayed in 3D
  • New Analysis screen: your slowest steps and cases, and the algorithms you use
  • New drills, to practise cases on your own cube
  • New AI coach: a weekly training plan written from your solves
  • The last cube can be reconnected automatically when the app opens
v2.1.1
  • 2x2 scrambles are now 11 moves using R, U and F only, like official ones
  • The history can now be sorted by best Ao5, Ao12, Ao50 or Ao100
  • Tapping an average in the solve details shows the solves it is made of
  • A session or an average can be copied with every solve\'s scramble, to paste anywhere
  • A time under half your personal best asks before it is saved as a record, in case the timer was stopped by mistake
  • New \"Last layer colour\" setting for scramble types such as Last layer, PLL or F2L
  • These notes can now be turned off after updates
v2.1.0
  • Cubench can now back up everything to a single file, to restore on another phone
  • A +2 now shows beside the time it was added to, and a DNF shows the time it replaced
  • New scramble type: Roux second block
  • Several settings have been renamed for clarity
  • Fixed screens dropping back to the main screen after Android had closed the app in the background
  • In the session bars, a DNF is drawn at the length of the time it replaced
v2.0.0
Cubench has been redesigned from top to bottom. Timer
  • The scramble now shows on the timer screen itself, in 3D or as a flat diagram (can be hidden in the settings)
  • While a solve runs, the screen keeps nothing but the time
  • The last 12 times are shown as bars (the times table is still available via the settings)
  • Records are now announced in a line instead of a popup, and so are the best and worst of your last 12
  • Inspection can now be turned on or off for specific solve types
History and solves
  • Customizable statistics fields in the history screen
  • History rows are led by the time and grouped by day
  • Solve details open as a sheet you can swipe from one solve to the next, and drag away to close
  • The scramble view and the cross solver can now also be opened from a solve\'s details
  • A DNF can be taken back, restoring the time it replaced (not retroactive)
Graphs
  • New \"Distribution\" graph, counting how many of your solves fall in each time range
  • Your last 50 solves now show up as a graph in the history screen, which leads to the graph screen when tapped
Misc
  • Help buttons on several screens explain what they show
  • \"Cube type\" is now called \"Puzzle type\"
  • Each puzzle type now has a color of its own, which follows it through the app
  • The export screen now groups your times by puzzle, showing how many solves each holds and how many you have picked
  • Random-state scrambles are now always used, so the switch and the screen of options behind it are gone
  • Settings use switches, and number settings offer presets instead of a scrolling wheel
  • Many smaller fixes and adjustments throughout
v1.4.3
  • The new record panel no longer covers the scramble
  • New setting to choose when the record panel appears: for any record, only for a new PB, or never
  • New \"Last solve\" menu entry on the timer screen, opening the solve details, where commenting and sharing have moved
  • Fixed the timer digits shifting around while timing on some devices
  • Megaminx scrambles no longer end with an empty line
  • Export can now save your history directly to a file, and sharing it works with more apps
  • Refreshed popups and dropdowns to match the rest of the app
v1.4.2
  • Portuguese translation
  • You can now rate Cubench from the menu, without leaving the app
v1.4.1
  • New record overlay showing your improvement and previous time(s)
  • Add settings to choose the timer font and its size
  • Add scrambles to manually entered times

  • Solve types can now be fully edited (scramble type, blind flag), not just renamed
v1.4.0
Nano Timer is now Cubench! (Same app, new name.)
New features
  • Scramble visualizer for all puzzles
  • New FTO cube type, with random-state scrambles
  • 3x3 cross solver: optimal cross solutions for any face and color-neutrality
  • \"Add time\" dialog now supports milliseconds and DNF entries

A Bluetooth smart cube reports every turn to Cubench as you make it. Once yours is paired, three things change.
Connect to this cube when the app opens
If the app thinks your cube is scrambled when it is not, the cube has lost track of itself. Solve it, then reset the state.
It starts on your first turn and stops the moment the cube is solved. No tapping, no missed starts.
Cubench watches you apply the scramble, marks off each move as it lands, and says when you are ready to go.
Cross, F2L, OLL and PLL are timed separately, with move counts, turn speed and the full reconstruction.
Give your cube a quarter turn to wake it up, and keep it near the phone.
Cubench needs Bluetooth switched on to find your cube.
Cubench needs permission to find nearby devices. It only ever looks for cubes, and nothing leaves your phone.
Cubench can no longer ask for this permission from here. Open the app settings and allow nearby devices.

Used to reconstruct your solves when a smart cube is connected: it tells the app which steps to break a solve into. Leave it on the default to follow the preferred method from the settings, or set it to the method you actually use for this solve type.
%1$d solves of this solve type were read as %2$s. They can be read again as %3$s, which can take a while on a long history. Nothing is lost: setting the method back and reading again restores them.
The method solve types are read as, unless they set their own
Stop the timer as soon as the cube reads solved, rather than on a tap
Give a solve stopped one move from solved a +2, and one stopped further out a DNF
Which method do you solve with? It is used to break your solves down into steps. This is the default, and each solve type can be set on its own.
The timer stopped and the time was saved. Discarding removes it.
Less than half your personal best of %1$s.
No solves yet. Press Start to time one.
Any of them can go in any of the three cells.
A statistic with a number in its name covers only that many of your most recent solves, so it moves with every solve you do.
Mean all is the plain mean of your times, DNFs left out. Acc all, on blind types, is how often you succeeded. Both look back over your whole history under this solve type, up to the last 1000 solves.
Your fastest ever under this solve type, however far back it is.
An average drops the fastest and the slowest, then means the rest. A mean drops nothing, so one DNF among its solves makes it a DNF.
Ao5 is not offered, since blind attempts are counted in threes. Acc says how often you succeeded, and an average counts successes only, reaching past a DNF rather than counting it.
An average here counts successes only: Ao12 is the average of your last twelve successful solves, reaching back past any DNF rather than counting it.

These figures come from your own solves, the ones a cube read, over the window shown at the top.
One block per step, as wide as its share of the time. Each block is pale where you were looking and solid where you were turning.
These are shares of one solve, so if one step is over, another has to be under. It shows which step is out of balance.
Mean, best and spread for each step. Tap a heading to sort by it. Steps that have named cases, OLL and PLL, show an arrow and open them.
How much the time changes from solve to solve. The same mean can come from doing it the same way every time, or from getting stuck now and then.
How you last turned each case of the set: with one of the algorithms listed for it, which is considered standard.
The turns those cases cost you over the shortest standard algorithm, added up.

Plans are part of the Cubench coach, a paid feature. The coach reads your smart cube solves, finds what costs you the most time, and turns it into a plan for the week, with drills for your weak points.
Up to three things to work on, the one worth the most first. Each says what is happening, why, and one thing to do about it.
The button on a focus opens a drill made for it. Each case leaves the drill once you have beaten its target a few times.
Under the plan, the cases costing you the most, ready to practise between plans.
Written from your last 100 smart cube solves, so the first one needs that many. After that a new plan comes every week, once you have done 25 more solves and your session is over.
The cases of the selected step that you put in with one algorithm, over the window shown at the top. Only those solves count: a time where you took two looks is left out.

Known went in with one algorithm and no help, recently enough for that to still hold. Needs review went in that way before, but took two looks the last two times. To learn has never gone in with one algorithm. All of it is read from your solves, not from a list you tick.
On OLL, a Shape button narrows the table to one group of shapes, with each group\'s size beside it.
Under the table, the cases that did not go in with one algorithm in the window, grouped by where they stand over all your solves. Tap one for its algorithms.
Nothing on these tabs is yours. These figures are made up, and they are here so the screen has something to show before you own a smart cube. Connect one and your own take their place.
